title: Fabrication of Size-Controlled and Emulsion-Free Chitosan-Genipin Microgels for Tissue Engineering Applications
protocol: Obtain purified and lyophilized low molecular weight chitosan from commercially available sources.
Add 495 mL of double-distilled water and a stir bar to a 1 L beaker.
Add 5 g of chitosan to the beaker containing double-distilled water.
Mix well to disperse the chitosan in the solution.
Add 5 mL of glacial acetic acid to the prepared chitosan solution.
Stir covered at 300 rpm for 18 h with the beaker set in a water bath held at 50 °C.
Filter the chitosan solution through decreasing sizes of filter paper: 22 μm, 8 μm, and 2.7 μm.
Add the filtered chitosan solution to cellulose dialysis tubing.
Allow to dialyze in double-distilled water at room temperature for 4 days, changing the double-distilled water every day.
Transfer the dialyzed chitosan solution to a beaker.
Adjust the pH to 8.0 using 1 M NaOH.
Aliquot the chitosan into centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 4000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Decant the supernatant to a waste stream.
Resuspend the chitosan in ddH2O, repeating twice.
Freeze and then lyophilize the chitosan pellet.
Remove the lyophilized product each day and record its mass.
Add 2 mL of 6% acetic acid to a 10 mL Luer-lock syringe.
Add 120 mg of purified chitosan to the syringe containing 6% acetic acid.
Mix the solution back and forth for 30 seconds until chitosan fully dissolves.
Add any therapeutic or bioactive agent to the chitosan solution if needed.
Mix SDF-1a and TGF-b3 with the chitosan solution thoroughly.
Prepare a 100 mM stock crosslinker solution of genipin in 100% ethanol.
Add 100 µL of the prepared genipin solution to the chitosan-containing syringe.
Mix the contents back and forth between syringes for 30 seconds.
Extrude the mixture from the syringe onto a 35 mm Petri dish.
Cover the Petri dish with paraffin film.
Incubate the dish at 37 °C overnight in a humidified atmosphere.
Gently break the hydrogel into small pieces using a spatula.
Place a filter of desired mesh size into the back of a clean 10 mL syringe.
Transfer the broken gel pieces into the syringe fitted with the filter.
Add 6 mL of ddH2O to the syringe containing the gel pieces.
Connect the syringe via a Luer-lock connector to another clean 10 mL syringe.
Force the gel + water mixture through the syringe with the filter.
Open the back of the syringe containing the filter and extrude the mixture back into this syringe.
Replace the back of the syringe and force the mixture through the filter again.
Repeat filtration of the gel mixture 5-6 times or until there is little resistance through the filter.
Transfer the filtered gel mixture to a 50 mL conical tube.
Bring the total volume up to 20 mL with ddH2O.
Vortex the mixture to ensure homogeneous dispersion.
Centrifuge the microgels at 100 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Decant the upper aqueous phase.
Resuspend the microgels in 10 mL of 70% ethanol.
Vortex the mixture.
Place under UV light for 1 h to sterilize.
Centrifuge the microgels at 1,000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the ethanol.
Rinse the microgels 3 times with ddH2O.
Resuspend the microgel pellets in a 1:1 ratio with ddH2O.
Store the resuspended microgels for up to 1 month at 4 °C if no bioactive agent is used; otherwise, use immediately.
Create the injury site in the animal according to a previously published report.
Flush the injury site with saline.
Either keep the animal untreated (for control study) or inject the chitosan microgels only or the microgels loaded with the bioactive agents.
Close the wound and administer post-surgical analgesics.
Euthanize the rat by CO2 overdose at days 7 or 28 post-surgery.
Excise the limbs and perform histology to assess tissue repair at the injury site.
